refuted.finding: Long package ids in the dialog list wrap in the middle of a word with no hyphen ('Abstracti|ons', 'Configuratio|n.EnvironmentVariables', 'Dependenc|yInjection', 'Logging.Abs|tractions', 'Con|figurationExtensions'), so the ids no longer read as identifiers; workbench dialogs and lists never split an identifier at an arbitrary character.
refuted.reason: The mid-word breaks are visible ('Abstracti|ons', 'Dependenc|yInjection'), but no rule, artboard element or measured exemplar covers how an identifier wraps (rubric §6: taste with no rule). The ids are live content and the layout around them holds (DS-OVERFLOW-6 'document 300×799 fits', hard). A token such as 'Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstractions:' has no break opportunity, so the workbench's own break-word wrapping would also split it at an arbitrary character, which contradicts the exemplar claim.

refuted.finding: The dialog's list wraps package ids in the middle of a word instead of at a dot or before the version ('Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstracti|ons', 'Configuratio|n.EnvironmentVariables', 'Dependenc|yInjection', 'Logging.Abs|tractions', 'Options.Con|figurationExtensions'), and leaves '→ 11.0.0' alone on its own line, so the ids are hard to read at 300 px. The artboard supplied is for main-installed-all and draws no such list, so I judged this against the identifiers themselves, not an artboard element.
refuted.reason: The crop shows the same mid-identifier wraps and '→ 11.0.0' on its own line. The second is ordinary wrapping at a space, and the first has no rule or artboard to cite; the judge admits the artboard draws no such list. Package ids are live content whose surrounding layout holds (DS-OVERFLOW-6 'document 300×799 fits', DS-TYPE-4 dialog-text description 18.2, both hard), so rubric §6 excludes the finding.

refuted.finding: The body message breaks the config path at the hyphen inside 'dense-workspace' ('.../fixtures/dense-' then 'workspace/nuget.config.'), so the line end reads like a typographic hyphenation inside a file name. A workbench confirm dialog keeps the path on one line or breaks it at a path separator.
refuted.reason: The crop shows the break after 'dense-' as described, but no rule or artboard element governs where a path wraps. The Sources dialog in the same run breaks the same path at the same hyphen, and the claim about a workbench dialog is not evidenced. This is taste with no rule (rubric §6).

refuted.finding: The confirmation is drawn over the bare page instead of over the Sources dialog: the band above and below the confirmation (y 297-327 and 476-506, where the same run's main-sources capture draws the NuGet sources dialog with its title, close button and nuget.org row) reads the plain scrimmed page (rgb 15/15/15 at 600,300 against 32/32/32 for the Sources surface), so the stacked layer the state's name promises is missing. The dialog that opened the confirmation, and that its focus should return to, is not shown.
refuted.reason: The bands above and below the confirmation do read as scrimmed page (15/15/15 at 600,300 and 600,490, against 32/32/32 for the Sources surface in main-sources). That hiding is by design: layers.ts marks every layer under the topmost one data-covered to give the workbench's single-modal look (one scrim, one box, UX-P3.6). The Sources dialog is still mounted, and focus returns to it when the confirmation closes.

refuted.finding: The confirmation's message "Removes the package reference from the project file." uses the noun "reference", which design-system §10 Microcopy item 7 forbids ("package (never reference, except 'Its reference could not be resolved.')"); the sentence should name the package only, e.g. "Removes the package from the project file."
refuted.reason: The crop does show the body text "Removes the package reference from the project file." inside the box, but the wording is a ruled design decision, not a defect. docs/design/DECISIONS.md row 2026-11-17 (design-advisor ruling, UX-P4.2a) fixes this exact body text for the dialog, which has no artboard. Here "reference" names the entry in the project file, as in the rule's own exception "Its reference could not be resolved."; it does not stand in for the package, so it falls outside §10 item 7. No hard measurement covers copy (DS-TYPE-4/dialog-text 18.2 and the other lines are green).
